companyDescription: Cell therapy · Deramiocel — allogeneic cardiac-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, first-in-class mechanism awaiting its second FDA decision (Nov 22)
priceNote: Live $8.02 (-2.7%) on Nov 4, 2026, up ~38% from $5.83 at the Oct 26 report. The stock jumped ~14% on Nov 3 after DMD clinical investigators publicly urged FDA approval. 52-week range $2.96-$40.37. Market cap ~$466M. Nov 4 tape: S&P futures -1.2% / Nasdaq -2% on a Democratic midterm sweep; Dec 9 hike ~85% priced.
summary: REFRESH (prior report Oct 26, 2026). The Nov 22, 2026 PDUFA for deramiocel, narrowed to upper-limb function in DMD (the HOPE-3 primary endpoint), is 18 days out. The stock has re-rated +38% since Oct 26, helped by the investigators' public letter to FDA (Nov 3, +14%) and the B. Riley upgrade (Buy, $21). fda_decision is a Tier-2 LEADER (+9.3pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=10). But the July adcomm voted 9-3 against efficacy on the original cardiomyopathy claim, and securities suits are pending, so this remains a two-sided binary. Base cut from +70% to +60% because some of the approval is now priced. It assumes approval on Nov 22 and a ~1-3 month move to ~$12.80, above the lane's realized 30-day P90 of +25.9% (Base bias +72.7pp). แนะนำ 2-3% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้าโดน CRL ลงได้ 50%+.

catalysts.name: Deramiocel PDUFA decision — upper-limb function indication
catalysts.description: FDA target action date for the amended BLA, narrowed to upper-limb function (PUL 2.0) after the Jul 29-30, 2026 adcomm voted 9-3 against the original DMD-cardiomyopathy claim. Clinical investigators publicly urged approval on Nov 3.

risks: The FDA adcomm voted 9-3 against efficacy for the original DMD-cardiomyopathy indication (Jul 2026, non-binding). The narrowed upper-limb ask is a reasonable fix, not an assured approval.
Part of the approval is now priced: +38% since Oct 26 and +14% on Nov 3 alone. The approval-day pop will be smaller than the Dec 2025 data move.
A second CRL (after the Jul 2025 CRL, -33% on day 1) would likely send the stock back to the ~$4 post-adcomm low and force a dilutive raise.
Securities class actions over the early-September 2026 disclosure are an overhang independent of the FDA outcome.
If approved, launch risk remains: payer coverage for a novel cell therapy, the narrower population, and manufacturing scale-up.

macroRisk.sectorImpact: Single-asset cell-therapy company. The FDA outcome dominates; rates matter through small-cap biotech risk appetite and the cost of a launch raise.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — the Nov 22 PDUFA lands between the Nov 10 CPI and the Dec 9 FOMC. A hot CPI would pressure small-cap biotech into the decision but doesn't change the binary.

catalystSpot.preRunup: A classic late pre-PDUFA run-up: +38% since Oct 26, capped by the Nov 3 investigator-letter pop (+14%), after a ~41% slide in October on litigation.

postWin.note: CAPR's own Dec 2025 HOPE-3 Phase 3 readout took the stock from $6.36 to $40.37 (+300%) in two trading days. An approval on the narrowed label, after the November run-up, likely produces a smaller move (+40-80%), but the stock has shown it can triple on this drug.

postLose.note: CAPR fell 36% on Jul 30, 2026 after the adcomm's 9-3 negative vote ($6.57 to $4.19), and 33% on day 1 of the Jul 2025 CRL. A second CRL would likely be at least as severe.

spotSizing.reason: 2.5%. fda_decision is a Tier-2 LEADER (+9.3pp vs +2.0pp, n=10), but the 9-3 adcomm, pending litigation and a +38% run-up keep it at 2.5%. The weak lane scoreboard (hitRate 4.9%, n=41) caps it here.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Wider than the fda_decision medianMAE (-18.4%, n=10). A break below ~$6.25 before Nov 22 suggests the market is pricing a second CRL.
